title: Territories
description: The territorial catalogue: the EU layer and, per jurisdiction, the navigation hubs and the regions (leaves) that edition files are written for. Territory is a canonical dimension, independent from the yearly editions. Three structural rules cannot be expressed here and are enforced in code: every region belongs to exactly one hub, a hub of a single region reuses that region's slug, and every hub member is a declared region of the same jurisdiction.

frozenOn.description: Date the catalogue was last settled. Territory changes rarely and deliberately, unlike the yearly editions.

principle.description: The territorial model in prose, kept with the data so it cannot drift from it.

jurisdictions.description: Keyed by ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, plus EU for the supranational layer. Not called countries because EU is not one.

jurisdiction.title: Jurisdiction
jurisdiction.description: A country, or the EU layer. The EU declares no hubs and no regions: it is inherited by every country and has no territory of its own here.

name.description: The jurisdiction's name in its own language, as it names itself.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 language the edition files of this jurisdiction are written in.

hubLabel.description: What this jurisdiction calls its hubs, in its own language and vocabulary.

leafLevel.description: The administrative or statistical level a leaf corresponds to, in this jurisdiction's own terms. Deliberately not a closed list: each jurisdiction names its own level.

leafLabel.description: What this jurisdiction calls its leaves, in its own language.

sources.description: Public pages that justify how this jurisdiction is divided. Empty only where there is no subnational territory to justify.

rationale.description: Why the division is drawn this way, in the jurisdiction's own language. A reader must be able to tell a documentary decision from an administrative fact.

hubs.description: Every navigation grouping of this jurisdiction. Empty for the EU layer, which has no territory of its own.

regions.description: Every documentary leaf of this jurisdiction, each belonging to exactly one of the hubs above.

url.description: The public page itself, over HTTPS.

authority.description: The body that publishes the page, named as it names itself.

purpose.description: What this source establishes about the division.

hub.title: Hub
hub.description: A navigation grouping. A hub of several regions may carry its own edition layer, which all its members inherit; a hub of one region is that region and never carries records of its own.

slug.description: Identifier of the hub, used in its URL and in the path of its edition file.

name.description: The hub's name in the jurisdiction's language, as readers see it.

members.description: Slugs of the regions in this hub. A single-member hub repeats that region's slug as its own.

region.title: Region
region.description: A documentary leaf: the smallest stable territory research coverage and records are assigned to.

slug.description: Identifier of the region, used in its URL and in the path of its edition and brief files.

name.description: The region's name in the jurisdiction's language, as readers see it.

inPhrase.description: The region's name as it reads inside a sentence in its own language, where that differs from the bare name.

parentHub.description: Slug of the one hub this region belongs to.

kind.description: Kind of territory where the region is not the jurisdiction's ordinary unit. In use: island, outre-mer, city-state, historical-territory, autonomous-region, autonomous-province. Open on purpose, because a further jurisdiction will bring its own kinds.

seoName.description: Longer name for page titles where the short name is ambiguous.

note.description: Anything a researcher or reader needs to know about this region that no other field holds, such as why its boundary differs from the administrative one.
